senses.definition: Lasting only a short time, and built that way on purpose.
senses.caution: In a technical room it is a claim rather than a description: say a workspace is ephemeral and the next questions are about the logs, the cache and whatever it wrote on its way out. Everywhere else it is a slightly literary word, elegant in writing and a little precious said out loud about a colleague's short tenure or a passing mood.
senses.example: Every agent run gets an ephemeral workspace — it exists for the task and nothing survives it.

cues.text: You are describing a design where each run gets a fresh environment that is destroyed the moment it finishes.
A security reviewer asks how long the credentials the agent uses stay valid, and the answer is nine minutes.
You are justifying why you do not want a permanent copy of the intermediate data kept anywhere.
You are telling a friend that the best thing about that festival is how the whole town it builds is gone by Monday.
You want a word for how quickly a mood of collective optimism came and went.

distractors: Safe to run more than once, because a second run changes nothing the first did not.
A basic building block a platform hands you and expects you to compose with.
Covering a wide range rather than a narrow one.
To put right something that was wrong.
The most senior people, taken as one group.
